summary: Tested the render-job pipeline (background job + polling) with 3 real AI generations: 1 single try-on via the API, 1 OutfitBuilder outfit via the UI and 1 OutfitGrid outfit via the UI. Backend: 15/15 pytest pass. POST returns {job_id, status:'running'} at once and GET /render-jobs goes running -> done with the doc. Errors come back with the original code and detail: 400, 402 quota, 403 foreign path, 404 and 422 for a bad retry reason. Another user's job returns 404 and no auth returns 401. The single try-on took about 60s and produced a 1536x2579 JPEG served as image/jpeg, with the white 'myatelierapp.it' signature and soft shadow at bottom-right. QC passed on the first attempt, so no fix pass was triggered. Frontend: the OutfitBuilder render (~33s) and OutfitGrid render (~42s) were polled through postRender and the result showed. The progress steps went 'Analizzo...' -> 'Sto provando...' -> 'Sistemo ... 2K' -> 'Controllo qualità: viso, mani e capi...'. The 'Salva in Galleria' button appears on TryOnDetail, the OutfitBuilder result and the OutfitGrid result. Clicking it downloads myatelier-<ts>.jpg (743KB) and shows the 'Foto salvata' toast. Two problems found: (1) the button text is almost invisible (grey on black), and (2) the single try-on output has flat grey letterbox bands with the signature sitting on the band.

critical.issue: SECURITY/IDOR: req.person_path and req.garment_path are never checked with _path_owner. Any logged-in user who knows a path can render another user's private avatar or photo, and the result is saved under the attacker. copylook/apply and generate-from-uploads do check ownership.

minor.issue: Quota race: because POST returns at once, a FREE user can start many jobs in parallel. Every job passes get_subscription_status before any consume_tryon_quota runs, so the user gets more renders than the limit. Fix: reserve or decrement the quota atomically when the job starts and refund on error, or allow at most 1 running job per user.

Jobs still running when the backend restarts or hot-reloads stay 'running' forever, and the client polls for 8 minutes before timing out. There is also no TTL index, so jobs and their full result docs pile up. Fix: on startup mark running jobs as error 500, and add a TTL index on created_at (e.g. 1 day).

In the single try-on (long dress), 548 of 2579 rows were flat grey padding at the top and bottom: the model did not extend the scene into the head_lock pad bands. The final photo looks letterboxed and the signature sits on the grey band, not on the photo. The outfit renders had no such bands. Consider trimming leftover flat pad bands before watermark(), or checking for them in QC.

ui_bugs.issue: Button label is unreadable. The .label-caps class sets color: var(--vfit-muted), which overrides text-white. Computed text is rgb(82,82,82) on a rgb(26,26,26) background, about 2.3:1 contrast. Seen on TryOnDetail (mobile) and the OutfitGrid result. Fix: drop label-caps, or use !text-white / inline style color:#fff.

issues: The 'Salva in Galleria' button is below the fold (y=1164), so the user has to scroll to find it. Consider also placing it in the right column near the actions.
Renders now finish in about 33-60s, so the 'Controllo qualità' step (shown at 70-88%) is often skipped or only shown briefly. This is cosmetic.

action_items: Fix the SaveToGallery text contrast (label-caps overrides text-white)
Add _path_owner checks for person_path and garment_path in /tryon/generate and for person_path in /outfit/generate
Make quota consumption atomic, or limit each user to 1 running render job
On startup, mark stale running render_jobs as errors and add a TTL index
Trim or avoid flat grey pad bands left in single try-on outputs before the watermark is applied
critical_code_review_comments: server.py is 3007 lines and should be split into routers (tryon, outfit, copylook, render jobs)
_start_render_job stores the whole result doc in render_jobs, which duplicates tryons/outfits data. Storing a ref id would be enough
_qc silently accepts the image when the QC LLM call fails (logs a warning). Acceptable, but no metric shows how often QC is skipped
postRender keeps polling on network errors until MAX_MS with no user feedback. Acceptable

success_rate.frontend: 90% (all flows work; save button contrast bug)
